data.title: A substrate-specific mTORC1 pathway underlies Birt-Hogg-Dube syndrome
data.authors: Napolitano G; Ballabio A et al.

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: A substrate-specific mTORC1-TFEB pathway (RagC/D-dependent) drives Birt-Hogg-Dube kidney disease.
data.abstract_excerpt: The mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1 (mTORC1) is a key metabolic hub that controls the cellular response to environmental cues by exerting its kinase activity on multiple substrates. However, whether mTORC1 responds to diverse stimuli by differentially phosphorylating specific substrates is poorly understood. Here we show that transcription factor EB (TFEB), a master regulator of lysosomal biogenesis and autophagy, is phosphorylated by mTORC1 via a substrate-specific mechanism that is mediated by Rag GTPases.

extracted_findings.effect: A substrate-specific mTORC1 pathway phosphorylates TFEB and underlies Birt-Hogg-Dubé syndrome
